newsitem.title: UK: China in 400,000 tpy financed alumina supply deal.
newsitem.headline: China in 400,000 tpy financed alumina supply deal.

text.p: Chinese state metals company, China National Nonferrous Metals Industry Corp, (CNNC) has agreed a 30 year deal commencing July 1997 to purchase 400,000 tonnes of alumina annually from Alcoa World Aumina (AWA).

A release from Credit Lyonnais Rouse Derivatives, arrangers of the transaction for its parent Crdit Lyonnais S.A., said financing involved a $180 million loan and revolving credit facility syndicated among 12 international banks.
It also included aluminium price hedging for a nominal $435 million over over five years and interest rate hedging over the 10 year loan period.

The transaction will assure a reliable supply of alumina to support China's domestic production of aluminium. This will relieve pressure on imported alumina which is currently running at approximately 1 million tonnes a year and typically concluded on a spot basis.
AWA, for its part, has secured long term rights to supply much of China's alumina shortfall without assuming financial exposure to the Chinese buyer, the release said.

Sino Mining Alumina Ltd, a subsidiary of CNNC's wholly owned investment vehicle, Sino Mining International Ltd made an upfront payment of $240 million to AWA on April 1 and has secured rights to increase the annual supply rate as CNNC's needs expand.
AWA is jointly owned by Aluminium Company of America Aluminum Co of America and WMC Ltd.
